title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive in an automated identification system that was escalated into a use of force. The license plate reader misread one character and returned a match to a stolen vehicle, and the alert was then acted on as though it were an identification. The failure sits at the handoff between the system's output and the officer's response, not in the camera alone.

What would have caught it is the step the vendor itself says is required: independent verification of an alert before enforcement. A single misread letter was enough to produce a stop at gunpoint, which means nothing between the alert and the drawn weapon tested whether the plate actually matched.

The cause of the misread is the sheriff's account, not an independent finding, and the claim that an illegal tinted plate cover produced it has not been established here. The department's judgment that the deputy's actions were reasonable is its own position, and no ruling on the stop appears in the reporting.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was reportedly held at gunpoint for more than five minutes after a Flock Safety license plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the malfunction and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said alerts should be independently verified before enforcement.
title_en: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover
